subject.title: message tool: Feishu send action polluted by poll schema/guard prevents file send

question: For plain `message.send`, should OpenClaw hide poll content fields from send-capable schemas, strip accidental poll fields at runtime, or keep rejecting content-bearing poll fields as explicit poll intent?
rationale: The remaining behavior affects the shared model-facing message-tool contract across channels, and the evidence supports multiple viable tradeoffs between send reliability and strict poll-intent validation.

options.title: Action-scope poll fields
options.body: Expose poll creation fields only for poll actions or a channel-specific poll tool so models are not invited to fill them during plain sends while strict poll validation remains intact.

options.title: Send wins and strips
options.body: Treat `action="send"` as authoritative and drop poll creation fields before delivery, maximizing send reliability but potentially hiding callers that meant to create a poll.

options.title: Keep strict content guard
options.body: Continue rejecting content-bearing poll fields on send and require stronger live evidence before changing the shared tool contract.

recommendation.title: Action-scope poll fields
recommendation.body: Expose poll creation fields only for poll actions or a channel-specific poll tool so models are not invited to fill them during plain sends while strict poll validation remains intact.

likelyOwner.reason: Their poll gating and schema-consistency commits are the strongest history signal for the shared send/poll contract boundary.
